mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized indicates inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) signals a slowdown in economic activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO decreases.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is below 2%, the real interest rate is positive, indicating a tightening monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is rising and the number of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) is decreasing, it signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE is rising and PAYEMS is decreasing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) indicates a contraction in economic activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 decreases.
